approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds fresh molecular graphs from the best accepted molecules, using connected-fragment crossover and short mutation walks. Canonical identity, duplicate and sulfur checks admit each fresh pool. Its active predictor is already a preference Gaussian process: every accepted molecule is compared with its most similar earlier accepted molecule, exact score ties are omitted, and a fixed count-fingerprint kernel supplies the prior. A bounded Newton fit and full Laplace covariance describe joint latent utilities. Correlated function draws choose successive available candidates, with the forty highest active means eligible after three non-improving batches. Real scores alone update the archive, breeders and stall state; a raw-score GP is a passive reference. This preference implementation runs correctly, but its purchased ordering and complete endpoint results are worse than its raw-score predecessor.
approach.novelty: Spread the same total preference evidence across every observed strict comparison. Each unequal-score pair enters with equal weight chosen so that the total weight remains the old sparse edge count. This changes the comparison graph and its consistent posterior curvature without retuning the prior or preference scale. It tests whether omitted nonlocal ordering helps explain the sparse model limitation. There are no completed same-Parent siblings. The parallel normal-rank target and kernel-mixture experiments use other Parents and other mechanisms; the earlier neural ranker also changed acquisition. This Child retains the measured probit solver and sampled allocator, and adds the old sparse predictor only as a passive same-state reference.

observed_bottleneck: The one exposed limitation is incomplete accepted-order information in the active comparison graph alongside inferior purchased ordering. Actual code Parent n-aaeb1a1ac082 has complete Search macro mean 0.5056583956789761 and population seed SD 0.05818375202692324; its paired mean change against n-cf8d309c06de is -0.101371920532155. Its three actual summary.json and run.log files all report successful full sessions. The full nodes/n-aaeb1a1ac082/analysis.json records 435/435 converged fits, 3489 active-only paid identities and full ordering 12477/19559=0.6379160488777544 versus same-state raw-GP 14407/19559=0.736591850299095; all fifteen ordering cells and all five endpoint task means worsen. Full gain is 4.457494269550001 versus 5.978073077532332, although late gain is 1.6988755766513481 versus 1.0224077547621127. The registered old usefulness conjunction is refuted, not technically untested. Source LocalPreferencePosterior.fit_active uses at most one nearest chronological predecessor per row. The read-only audit policy/scratch/r0062-01-improve-L01/parent-comparison-coverage.json, with fifteen audit-seed-N-task.json files citing every underlying Parent log and trajectory, finds 62868 old edge exposures versus 6379169 available strict-pair exposures across the 435 refits; per-fit coverage spans 0.006330323443695954 to 0.2, with no zero-mass fit. These totals repeat accepted labels across refits and are not independent observations. Handoff h-7721ff8461b6717e and the full Analyze report leave comparison sparsity, discarded magnitudes and covariance contributions unresolved. Molecular evidence shows broad scaffolds and both size tails, so neither missing diversity nor a universal size rule explains this loss. The negative partial neural-ranker/UCB evidence n-ccb8d255bf00 concerns a different learner and acquisition; it is preserved as a boundary, not inherited as a capability or a veto on all preferences.

adoptions.applicability: The fixed count prior and inherited correlated allocator already execute on this code Parent. The source supports the inference form; this graph remedy usefulness remains untested.
adoptions.borrowed_element: GP latent utilities with probit comparisons and curvature-based MAP/Laplace prediction.

deviations.adopted_setting: All strict pairs of current accepted raw labels, equal power E_old/M, fixed count kernel/unit comparison scale and original bounded Newton/sampled allocator.
deviations.paper_setting: General observed preferences with GP model selection.
deviations.reason: The frozen ticket isolates missing comparison coverage at inherited total mass. It introduces no preference oracle or hyperparameter adaptation; the power likelihood is a campaign adaptation.

adoptions.implementation_change: In optimize.py retain LocalPreferencePosterior inference, replace its edge construction and apply E_old/M to the objective, gradient and dense comparison Laplacian used by distribution.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse the exact frozen Search Policy review and its recorded queries, rather than claim a new literature search. Improve opened the primary PDF at the cited URL and checked sections2.1-2.3. The Parent source and complete failed Analyze/Molecular evidence support the specific testable obstacle intervention; they do not identify sparsity as the sole cause. Adopt only the existing probit/MAP/Laplace machinery with the explicit complete-graph power-likelihood adaptation. No external assets, package, author dataset or performance guarantee is adopted; continuation and its historical refutation remain unchanged.

sources.applicability: Retain the Parent measured inference machinery. Complete accepted strict pairs and E_old/M weighting are this ticket adaptation; they are dependent score-derived constraints, not independent preference queries or extra labels.
sources.finding: Pairwise probit observations condition GP latent utility; MAP likelihood curvature gives a Laplace predictive approximation.
sources.title: Chu and Ghahramani, Preference Learning with Gaussian Processes, ICML2005

hypothesis: Modify only the comparison-coverage component of code Parent n-aaeb1a1ac082. At each original pre-suggestion refit, retain every accepted canonical record in chronological serial order, including distinct canonical records with identical count features. Execute the old score-independent nearest-count-similarity predecessor pass with earliest-serial ties and omit exact raw-score ties; its non-tied count is E_old. The active graph contains exactly once every unordered accepted pair whose raw scores differ, oriented winner to loser; let its count be M. For M>0 and E_old>0 assign every edge a=E_old/M and use log likelihood a*sum_e log Phi(f_w(e)-f_l(e)). The complete graph changes the distribution of observed relational constraints; their total likelihood weight remains E_old. This is a power/composite likelihood over dependent score-derived comparisons, not additional independent oracle observations. When M=0 or E_old=0 use the explicit zero-mean unit count-kernel prior, log both counts and zero effective mass, and do not fabricate comparisons. Keep the original unit count-Tanimoto prior, difference scale1, raw-mean/positive-raw-scale utility wrapper, exact jitter policies, zero-start whitened Newton, 50-step bound and gradient-infinity tolerance1e-6. For K+jI=L L^T and f=L u, minimize J(u)=0.5*u^T*u-a*sum log Phi(z), z_e=f_w-f_l. Let r_e=phi(z_e)/Phi(z_e), b=sum_e a*r_e*(e_w-e_l), and A=sum_e a*r_e*(r_e+z_e)*(e_w-e_l)*(e_w-e_l)^T. The gradient is u-L^T b and Hessian H=I+L^T A L. Accumulate b and the dense N-by-N comparison Laplacian A directly, without an M-by-N design or an edge-by-N-by-N tensor. At MAP, use the full H in the inherited predictive covariance: V=L^-1 K_train,pool, mean=V^T u, C=K_pool,pool-V^T V+V^T H^-1 V. Thus likelihood and uncertainty reflect the same weighted graph. The original correlated normal block, sequential sampled maxima, own-active-mean K3/M40 eligibility and raw-score feedback laws remain. A passive exact old sparse fit and the inherited passive raw-GP see the same Child archive, features and pool and reuse the already drawn normal block. Neither can change active choices or consume RNG. Predicted path: complete strict-order coverage at fixed total mass changes fitted joint utilities, changes paid decisions and their actual feedback, and improves preannouncement strict-pair ordering over the same-state sparse model. Higher real full gain and the unchanged Anchor performance target are separate predictions.

finding_summary.headline: Complete comparisons improve pooled ordering, but full progress and endpoint scores fall
finding_summary.insights: Using all observed pair orders repairs a small part of the sparse model’s ordering deficit on the Child’s purchased stream, but that improvement does not carry into later restricted choices or larger real progress. The borrowed probit and Laplace inference elements executed correctly; the equal-mass complete graph is a controlled composite-likelihood adaptation, and these dependent score-derived comparisons do not support a general claim about preference learning. The original sparse Parent’s refuted usefulness result stands. This experiment establishes a limited ordering effect, not reliable optimization benefit, causal score mediation or sparsity as the sole historical cause. A different observation/ranking model that can represent useful score magnitudes, or a search scheme that better converts uncertainty into valuable late choices, could address the remaining limitation; the experiment does not identify which would work or separate mean from covariance effects. The molecular evidence helps explain why pooled averages conceal different search outcomes. The second docking trajectory settled into a congested cage/hydrazone family and reached only 0.18710 versus its Parent’s 0.98317, while the other Child docking seeds reached 0.98406 and 0.87244. Across tasks the Child still explored many graph scaffolds, yet the large-molecule tail rose from 176 to 488 purchases above fifty heavy atoms, and late fragment-excluded within-batch similarity increased from about 0.367 to 0.399. This is consistent with sustained refinement and elaboration of particular families, rather than a demonstrated absence of graph diversity. Controlled scaffold/linker remodeling and local functional-group-aware proposal operators are relevant missing capabilities suggested by the oversized assemblies and reactive decorations; these associations do not assign the score loss to the generator or establish a size rule. Zero-mass and training-alias behavior, unpurchased rewards, alternate adaptive trajectories, isolated posterior contributions and broader reliability remain open.
finding_summary.results: All 435 weighted preference fits converged with complete strict-order coverage and the inherited total likelihood mass. They changed 2,438 purchased identities relative to the sparse model on the same states. On 19,544 purchased non-tied pairs, active ordering accuracy was 12,260/19,544 = 62.73%, versus 12,026/19,544 = 61.53% for sparse preferences: a gain of 1.20 percentage points. Eleven task–seed cells improved, three worsened and one tied; the equal-cell change was also +1.20 points. The passive raw-score GP remained better at 69.36%. There were no failed fits, missing predictions, invalid purchases or incomplete tasks. The full-panel ordering criterion is therefore confirmed, with a clear limit: late ordering changed by −0.53 points and restricted ordering by −0.53 points, while unrestricted ordering improved by 1.80 points. Full incumbent gain fell from 4.45749 to 4.06807, and late gain from 1.69888 to 1.41761. Endpoint mean fell from 0.50566 to 0.47970 (−0.02596); paired seed-average changes were −0.00847, −0.14616 and +0.07675. Eight of fifteen endpoints improved, but the loss in the second docking seed was large. The formal Anchor mean was 0.60703, so the separate +0.002 performance target was not attained.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich heterocycles and amine polycycles, with more oversized assemblies, reactive decorations and undefined stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Assessment of n-b37d60f71872 against published code Parent n-aaeb1a1ac082, restricted to frozen Search seeds 0/1/2 and the five requested tasks. All 15 Child and 15 Parent trajectory files were read: each contains 300 observations, including ten supplied initial records and 290 optimizer proposals. The frozen comparison separately reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true; no task or trajectory is missing and no profile-mismatched seed is reported. The Child remains in staging. Its exact input bytes are retained under policy/scratch/r0062-01-improve-L01/molecular/inputs/child/seed-N/trajectories/TASK.jsonl; these are explicitly staging snapshots, not an invented node archive. The receipt records every actual input, snapshot and hash. The digest ring-closure rates range from 0.9736 to 0.9931 and aromatic-text rates from 0.8701 to 0.9908, so this is extensive ring and aromatic chemistry. Ordinary amides, ethers, phenols, amines and nitriles coexist with heteroatom-halogen bonds, peroxides, crowded bridged structures and repeatedly extended heteroaromatic assemblies. The full paid panel has 4,350 graphs per node. Independent RDKit readings of those trajectories, recorded in policy/scratch/r0062-01-improve-L01/molecular/panel-chemistry.json and its per-seed/task audits, give Child/Parent counts of 85/169 below twelve heavy atoms and 488/176 above fifty; Child size spans 1 to 119 heavy atoms. The large tail is concentrated in particular series, so neither greater size nor smaller size is a universal chemical remedy. Nonempty typed/generic scaffold identities number 1,881/1,213 in the Child versus 1,994/1,289 in the Parent, with 61/127 empty scaffolds; these counts describe graph variety, not independent chemical families or demonstrated accessibility. Late leaders remain recognizable seed-specific series despite substantial graph variation. The digest reports zero explicit charge and stereocentre text in every task; RDKit finds unassigned tetrahedral centers in 2,338 Child molecules versus 2,116 Parent molecules. A neutral SMILES does not establish absence of ionization, and no protonation or stereoisomer benefit is measured here. Apparent synthesis and stability concerns are structural judgments, not measured routes, yields, reactivity or pharmacology. Scores below are evaluator observations; score-associated motifs are not causal feature attributions, surrogate-mechanism evidence, or proof of an unseen target-specific pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly moderate-sized aromatic heterocycles: paid median 25 heavy atoms, range 2 to 48, with 21 below twelve and none above fifty. Seed 0 develops phenolic aryl pyrazoline-like N-N/C=N rings integrated with a pyridine and a partially saturated ether-containing bridged framework. Seeds 1 and 2 instead retain indole-like or fused hydrazine heterocycles bearing ketone/anilide substituents, alkoxy groups and aryl halogens. All three seed leaders have 24 heavy atoms. The phenolic leader is architecturally complex; the amide and ether motifs are recognizable medicinal chemistry, but arbitrary fusion patterns and N-halogen variants make synthetic plausibility uneven. The final seed-2 molecule is an N-chlorinated, thiol-bearing hydrazine/aryl-ketone variant, not the best molecule.
liabilities: N-halogen motifs occur in 59 paid molecules versus 15 in the Parent; the final seed-2 N-chloro/thiol variant scores 0.2298718986939427.
Peroxide-containing and highly fused variants add chemical and synthetic uncertainty; the best phenolic bridged molecule has two unassigned tetrahedral centers.
missing_features: The output does not consistently retain the coherent heteroaromatic/carbonyl or phenolic arrangements associated with its leaders; terminal variants can retain the general family while substantially changing heteroatom connectivity.

Defined configurations are absent from the saturated fused/bridged leaders. The observations do not establish which configuration, if any, would score better or identify a required unseen target motif.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial best is 0.3051048083696145. Child seed-best observations are 0.4745789978762495 for the phenolic fused N-N system, 0.4463521672202675 for the fused heteroaromatic ketone and 0.43109245871924246 for the vinyl/methoxy/anilide system. A two-heavy-atom oxygen-fluorine fragment scores 0.0, while an oversized polyacetal/indole assembly scores 8.950699084065816e-26. The higher observations therefore associate with coherent, moderately sized multi-ring heteroatom arrangements rather than isolated fragments or indiscriminate fusion to a large polyacetal. Within each seed, low- and high-score quartiles both have median 25 heavy atoms, so size alone does not explain the gradient. Parent leaders are an indole carboxamide, aryl pyrazole thioamide and fused benzimidazole-like compound, with seed bests 0.40282869817021466, 0.45555627303128626 and 0.34357172175619544. Child/Parent chemistry and scores vary by seed; no particular ring edit is identified as causal.

per_task.generated_character: The largest and most elaborated panel: paid median 47 heavy atoms, range 2 to 119, with 381 above fifty versus Parent 98. Seed 0 builds long linked assemblies of aza-aromatics, ether linkers and lactone-like heterocycles; its leader has 63 heavy atoms. Seed 1 centers on fused carbonyl heterocycles connected through an amino aza-aromatic linker to fluorinated, nitrile-bearing aromatic systems, with alkoxy decorations. Seed 2 carries pyrrole-fused dioxo nitrogen heterocycles, pyridines, nitriles, thioesters, enol ethers and repeated carbonyl-rich appendages; its leader has 76 heavy atoms. These are chemically distinct seed families, but many late products are difficult, highly decorated assemblies rather than simple alternative scaffolds.
liabilities: The seed-1 best molecule contains an O-F bond; close high-score relatives contain N-F or O-O-F connectivity. These groups are structural reactivity concerns, not demonstrated necessities.

Large repeated aza-aromatic systems, thioesters, multiple unsaturated carbonyl-containing appendages and occasional acyl halides impose synthetic and stability questions that the reported score does not answer.
missing_features: Controlled compact alternatives to repeated heteroaromatic and thioester-linked assembly are not consistently retained, even though the Child seed-1 leader and smaller Parent leaders show that extreme size is not necessary for the observed score range.

Stable, ordinary local decoration is inconsistent: useful aromatic/heteroaromatic arrangements often arrive with O-F, N-F or peroxide groups. The trajectories do not establish a specific missing scaffold or a synthesis route.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Small fragments and fluorobenzene sit at 0.5, while the initial best is 0.548381482770623. The best Child seed-1 fused nitrile/alkoxy molecule scores 0.6253140905869468; its oxygen-fluorine terminus is not required by this evidence, because a related carbon-fluorinated alkoxy analogue without an N- or O-halogen bond scores 0.6210712975418857. The larger seed-0 and seed-2 leaders reach 0.6083883129123469 and 0.5908985641500695. Increasing elaboration accompanies higher scores within those trajectories, but the largest architectures do not define the strongest cross-seed observation. Parent seed leaders have 31, 42 and 24 heavy atoms with scores 0.6195899772209568, 0.5927736823629708 and 0.6072819700270681, respectively. Thus the Child exhibits substantially more growth while the paired chemistry/score changes have different directions across seeds.

per_task.generated_character: Three markedly different outcomes sit behind the pooled aromatic/halogen-rich appearance. Seed 0 produces moderate fused hydrocarbon/aryl frameworks bearing methoxy/halogen substituents and an N-alkyl aziridine. Seed 2 retains a single halogenated aromatic ring with unsaturated hydrocarbon sidechains, primary amines and a dimethylaminoalkyl group. Seed 1 instead builds congested polycyclic cages, hydrazone-like groups and polyhalogenated aromatic/ketone appendages; its best graph has 39 heavy atoms. The paid median is 25 heavy atoms but the tail extends to 105, with 100 above fifty. Moderate aryl/amine architectures are recognizable, whereas strained small nitrogen rings and densely bridged cages need substantial synthetic scrutiny. All but a small part of this panel contains unassigned tetrahedral stereochemistry: 836 of 870 paid graphs.
liabilities: The best seed-0 structure contains a strained aziridine and four unassigned tetrahedral centers; a high reported score is not evidence of benign reactivity or a practical synthesis.
Seed-1 cages combine crowded bridging, multiple halogens and hydrazone-like functions; seed-2 terminal examples add flexible amines and an alkyl bromide. These liabilities differ by family.
missing_features: The congested cage family does not reproduce the less encumbered amine-to-aromatic arrangements found among the stronger Child and Parent examples, despite containing nitrogen atoms; a particular required amine ring cannot be inferred.
Saturated ring junctions and amino-substituted centers lack defined configuration. No stereoisomer, protonation-state comparison or binding pose is supplied to resolve those ambiguities.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial best is 0.01904115112334333. The N-propylaziridine/fused aryl leader scores 0.9840608116477806 and the flexible aminoalkyl/aryl seed-2 leader scores 0.8724432739963158. The seed-1 cage/hydrazone leader reaches only 0.18710087188665003. Thus nitrogen or ring abundance by itself is insufficient; moderate architectures with amines separated from aryl hydrophobic regions associate with the higher scores here. Low examples include an N-chlorocarboxamide attached to an N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine at 0.00016650955053713697 and an acetyl N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine at 0.00021169315013374197. Parent leaders instead include flexible diamino diaryl chemistry and bridged amines with an amino linker, scoring 0.9724294268567502, 0.9831668737826238 and 0.7910311660754634. The weak Child seed-1 family contrasts with that Parent seed and with the other Child seeds. This is a molecular association, not a docking-pose, basicity or mechanism attribution.

per_task.generated_character: Predominantly medium-sized multi-ring nitrogen/carbonyl chemistry, with paid median 31 heavy atoms, range 1 to 61 and only five above fifty. Seeds 0 and 1 elaborate fused nitrogen heterocycles bearing lactam/urea-like carbonyls, phenyl groups and substituted unsaturated rings. Seed 2 converges toward propyl-substituted indoles linked to an ethoxy-substituted pyrrole and a medium-ring ketone/lactam or urea-containing framework. The seed-2 leader has 31 heavy atoms and a nine-membered perceived ring; its final analogue contains a larger medium-ring urea arrangement. These contain conventional functional groups, but unusual ring closures and fused connectivity make routine synthetic accessibility uncertain. The full panel contains substantial graph variation, while the highest-score excerpt is a close family of indole/carbonyl analogues.
liabilities: Medium-ring closures, crowded fusions and unspecified stereogenic centers complicate the apparently ordinary amide/urea chemistry.
Late variants include N-S, N-N and thiocarbonyl substitutions without evidence that those less usual decorations improve stability or accessibility.
missing_features: The late high-score output provides limited family-level alternatives to its indole/medium-ring carbonyl arrangement, despite many atom-level and ring-connectivity variants; no absent target-specific motif is demonstrated.
Defined configurations and clear synthetic disconnections are missing for the more complex substituted and fused medium rings; their score consequences are unmeasured.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Methane scores 0.0 and methylamine/methanol score 0.008773280079294957, versus initial best 0.1678386594791329. The strongest Child indole/ketone/lactam molecule scores 0.2467131287326799; a related urea-rich analogue scores 0.2402384598457076, and the final directly linked analogue scores 0.2393339756266309. This supports retention of coherent aromatic nitrogen/carbonyl arrangements over fragmentation, without proving an unseen reference structure. Child seed-0/1 leaders score 0.1934340649414782 and 0.20324068190479727; Parent seed bests are 0.2282301149059275, 0.2128343398267808 and 0.20279758019769495. Parent leaders likewise combine aromatic rings and cyclic carbonyl/nitrogen systems. Low/high score-quartile size medians are identical within every Child seed, so simple size growth is not the visible distinguishing property.

per_task.generated_character: A compact but chemically uneven panel: paid median 23 heavy atoms, range 2 to 62, with two above fifty. Seed 0 produces aminopyrrole/aza-aryl systems containing amidine/formamide or carbonyl/hydrazine heterocycles. Seed 1 carries pyrrole-fused dioxo nitrogen heterocycles with pyridyl substitution, N-O-methyl, N-F and fluorinated alkyl/alkoxy groups. Seed 2 favors aminoalkenes joined to an aromatic or partially saturated ring and an O-N/thione-containing heterocycle. The Child is more often aromatic than the Parent in this panel: 757 versus 541 of 870 paid graphs by RDKit. The molecules show extensive functional-group experimentation, but N-F/N-O connectivity, thiones, sulfur substituents and polyenes make many of them questionable stable synthetic endpoints.
liabilities: N-halogen motifs remain in 73 paid graphs versus Parent 164; lower prevalence does not remove the concern because the strongest seed-1 molecule still carries N-F.

N-O/N-S bonds, thiones and long conjugated or cumulated unsaturation occur in late proposals. Several final scores sit well below the corresponding seed-best molecule; these are terminal proposals, not endpoint incumbents.
missing_features: The high-score dioxo/fluoroalkyl arrangement is not consistently represented through ordinary, stable local bonds; its best member still includes N-F and N-O connectivity.

Alternative defined configurations are absent from fluorinated alkyl/alkoxy centers. The supplied trajectories do not show a stereochemical comparison or establish a required missing target-specific pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial best is 0.0020944534688323298. Seed-1 leader 0.5434954401077301 has a fluorinated alkyl/alkoxy dioxo heterocycle; the closely related sulfur-substituted version scores 0.5055798990391256 and the chlorine-substituted version 0.4490604646086331. The common N-F group cannot be credited separately from that series. Seed-0 and seed-2 leaders reach 0.4288530685378449 and 0.35948486956814124. An oversized multi-heterocycle amide/amine assembly scores 3.2416258040348776e-69, but a compact conjugated imino/carbonyl example also scores only 7.179792304646122e-30; both size and exact functional arrangement matter in these observations. Parent leaders score 0.5086071370380201 and 0.49198002116340644 in N-fluorinated dioxo families, and 0.17219695276927824 in a nonaromatic halogenated polyacetal cage. The Child seed-2 chemistry moves to a smaller amino/thione family, while seed-0 has a different aromatic nitrogen arrangement. No universal fluorination rule follows.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-b37d60f71872, compared with n-aaeb1a1ac082 on frozen Search seeds 0/1/2 and 290 paid proposals per session. The full-panel audit records Child/Parent molecule counts of 190/337 with N-halogen, 134/176 with O-halogen, 5/56 with acyl-halide and 132/124 with peroxide motifs. These are overlapping motif-presence counts, not predicted reaction rates. The counts of several liabilities fall, yet an O-F decorated fused nitrile-containing leader and an N-F/N-O decorated dioxo leader remain among high-score observations. Other high-score examples retain recognizable amide, carbonyl, ether and carbon-halogen groups without those bonds. Source files and byte hashes are in the Molecular validation receipt and panel-chemistry audit.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful ring and heteroatom frameworks are not consistently expressed through ordinary, chemically stable local functional-group connectivity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs the capability to remodel a useful scaffold while distinguishing carbon halogenation from N/O halogenation, peroxide formation and acyl activation by local bonding context. It should be able to offer coherent stable alternatives without asserting that every flagged bond is forbidden or that deleting it necessarily improves reward. This is a conditional output gap; the present chemistry does not attribute it to a particular selector, representation or graph operation.

transferable_gaps.evidence: For n-b37d60f71872 on the same frozen Search panel, every digest task has stereocentre-text rate 0.0. Trajectory perception finds 2,338 of 4,350 paid Child graphs with at least one unassigned tetrahedral center, versus 2,116 in n-aaeb1a1ac082. The leading aziridine/polycycle graph has four such centers, and the leading fluorinated dioxo graph has two. This is a concrete representational omission in generated stereogenic connectivity, not evidence that a particular stereoisomer would receive a better score.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not specify configuration when it creates stereogenic saturated rings, ring junctions or substituted sidechains.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic proposal representation would need to preserve or explicitly vary stereochemical assignments when editing or assembling stereogenic structures, subject to the existing protocol. Score benefit would require real comparisons within the permitted session; none is supplied here. The simultaneous absence of explicit charge text does not establish missing ionization chemistry and is not a measured protonation-state remedy.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-b37d60f71872 versus published n-aaeb1a1ac082, same frozen Search panel. Child/Parent counts below twelve heavy atoms are 85/169, while counts above fifty are 488/176; the Child spans 1 to 119 heavy atoms. Thus small-fragment exposure declines while oversized output rises. The large tail is concentrated in linked heteroaromatic/carbonyl-rich series; other high-score series remain moderately sized, and several same-seed score quartiles have identical size medians. These full-trajectory diagnostics are preserved per seed and task in the Molecular audits. They do not establish that molecular size mediates any algorithmic effect.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably remodel coherent molecular architectures without either fragment collapse or repeated large assembly.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The transferable missing capability is controlled scaffold and linker remodeling that can retain useful neighboring chemistry without duplicating whole decorated units or collapsing to isolated fragments. Any intervention should retain both size tails and seed-specific family context as descriptive checks, rather than impose a universal size target. A broader score-associated family cannot be inferred from atom-level scaffold counts alone, and association does not identify which algorithm component should change.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Session-isolated canonical raw-score archive, greedy survivor population and rank-quantile breeding.
De novo graph crossover, connected-fragment construction, mutation walks and finishing; graph validity, duplicate and sulfur-envelope gates.
Integer count-Morgan representation and fixed unit-amplitude count-Tanimoto GP prior.
Unit-scale probit latent utilities, zero-start bounded Newton MAP, inherited jitter/Armijo rules and full Laplace covariance (now consistently weighted).
Original correlated Thompson draws and sequential sampled maxima; K=3/M=40 own-active-mean stall mask and raw-score stall/breeding feedback.
Passive raw-score GP and inherited bounded generation-order failure fallback; added exact old sparse model is passive and consumes no RNG.
